operating_cash_reserve.note: Model assumption sized on full-year continuing operating revenue. The 2.5% base rounds the $2,091 million calendar 2025 nine-month working-capital cash use divided by $82,463 million calendar 2025 continuing revenue. The historical cash flow statement includes the pre-spin Freight business, so this is a calibration proxy. CY2026 nine-month operating expenses less D&A average about $220 million per calendar day and provide a second scale check. At the CY2026 revenue outlook the base is about 10.5 days of this cost proxy. The 2.0% to 3.5% cases cover about 8 to 15 days at the same reference scale. This reserve is a liquidity floor, distinct from annual operating working-capital movements. Deduct it once from cutoff cash. If rolled with revenue, account for incremental funding once in operating cash flow. The available revolver supports liquidity and contributes no cash to the bridge. FedEx states most foreign cash is accessible without material tax. No separate accessible balance or repatriation cost is disclosed.

fdxf.note: Use the dated public close and the last verified exact beneficial share count. The September 10-Q confirms the reported 19.9% stake and states that management expects to monetize it within 12 months of September 30 subject to market conditions. Spin documentation contemplates exchanging shares to retire FedEx debt, distributing them to stockholders, or exchanging them for FedEx shares. The base credits the gross marked asset and books no separate sale proceeds, tax, discount or fee. The 10% downside is an analyst proceeds stress, not an estimate of a tax rate or transaction discount. If a monetization scenario is modeled, release the corresponding retained asset once against cash, debt retirement or distribution. Keep valuation gains and losses on the equity security outside core FCFF.

inpost.note: Use the recent FedEx cash contribution and reported equity-method carrying value as the base proxy for its private TopCo interest. InPost's May position statement separately identifies the initial FedEx commitment of up to EUR 2,176 million, consistent with FedEx's rounded EUR 2.2 billion contribution. The tender was for InPost shares. FedEx owns 37% of TopCo, whose consortium financing combines committed equity and debt. Gross tender equity multiplied by 37% ignores the vehicle's capital structure. Later debt launches and the InPost bond tender provide refinancing context without establishing final net debt or the TopCo stake's fair value. The sensitivity applies a hypothetical 10% change in InPost equity to the tender price anchor, then multiplies by the offeror's announced 98.49% ownership, FedEx's 37% TopCo interest and September 30 USD/EUR. It holds vehicle financing, structure and FX constant and represents neither a current quote nor a liquidation estimate. September cash already reflects the purchase. Keep the investment, its earnings and distributions outside core operating value when the stake is added here. No additional FedEx contribution was quantified by the cutoff.

other_assets.note: Add the $266 million available-for-sale debt securities at September carrying fair value after excluding them from operating prepaids and from any definition of cutoff cash. Use $576 million carrying value for other equity securities, separately from InPost and FDXF. The May mix confirms that many of these securities are measured at cost subject to impairment and observed transactions, or at NAV. September category-level marks and an updated cutoff value are unavailable. The current swap asset and long-term swap liability are already carried in analytical balance-sheet accounts. Flag the net swap liability for sensitivity, with any separate valuation adjustment coordinated with working capital and modeled hedge flows. Aircraft deposits are operating assets tied to capex commitments.

contingencies.note: The disclosed customer obligation is offset against cash once. Do not infer a residual owned cash amount by subtracting the outstanding payable from cumulative CBP receipts. Additional tariff claims, customer lawsuits and collectibility have uncertain outcomes and no separately quantified net exposure in the 10-Q. The distinct $249 million tax-litigation benefit is cumulative recorded accounting exposure subject to appeal, with cash timing and final outcome unresolved. The May pension and healthcare values predate the pilot CBA remeasurement and are context only. The forecast already deducts modeled pension funding. Operating self-insurance accruals remain within the operating model. The Supply Chain deferred benefit is an accounting basis adjustment and does not establish final sale cash tax.

classification_notes: Use the modeled November cutoff cash net of tariff pass-throughs and accrued October cash movements, then subtract the required operating cash reserve. The October 1 dividend and October 1 Supply Chain proceeds already flow through the cutoff cash bridge.

Subtract modeled note and finance lease debt at the cutoff. Operating leases stay in operating expenses and therefore outside the debt deduction. Debt proceeds, the Freight dividend and July tender completed before the September balance sheet are already reflected in opening balances.

Value retained FDXF, InPost and other investments separately from operating value. Use the current FDXF market mark in place of the September carrying balance. Use the recent InPost investment and other September securities balances as marked or carrying proxies as documented.

Keep Supply Chain sale proceeds in cutoff cash only. Remove disposed assets and liabilities at sale. Avoid adding the transaction value, held-for-sale net assets or accounting gain to equity a second time.

FDXF disposition taxes or expenses, TopCo post-settlement leverage and shareholder commitments, precise repatriation costs, unquantified litigation and final disposal taxes remain evidence gaps. The bridge does not assign incremental amounts without a supportable dated cash estimate.
